documents: Chafik, Holliday, Bacon & Rossby (2022), Irminger Sea Is the Center of Action for Subpolar AMOC Variability, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL099133 (published PDF, 11 pp.; Supporting Information not supplied)

entry.evidence: our understanding of how the overturning circulation has evolved in the wider North Atlantic cannot be deduced from a single metric

sequences.source_document: Chafik et al. 2022, GRL, published PDF

steps.action: The authors pose the question of the subpolar AMOC signature, grounded in direct OSNAP East estimates, and set the aims: test it in a reanalysis, build a long-term indicator and probe the mechanism.
steps.quote: The objectives of this study are thus to reveal the signature of subpolar AMOC variability at its dominant source between Greenland and Scotland

steps.action: They take the OSNAP East AMOC time series (maximum of the overturning stream function in density space, 2014–2018) together with EN4 hydrography and CMEMS altimetry, and filter them with a 12-month Butterworth filter.
steps.quote: We use the maximum transport of the overturning stream function as observed at OSNAP

steps.action: They correlate OSNAP East AMOC with gridded 0–1,000 m density and sea-surface height, and find that a stronger AMOC coincides with denser water and lower SSH, centred on the Irminger Sea.
steps.quote: increased subpolar AMOC on interannual timescales is strongly associated with increased 0–1,000 m densities and decreased sea-surface heights in the Irminger Sea

steps.action: They compare Irminger Sea density sections in AMOC+ and AMOC− periods and find that the 27.55–27.7 isopycnals (the AMOC maxima) shoal west of the Reykjanes Ridge.
steps.quote: The density structure in the Irminger Sea is revealing of a pronounced shoaling of the 27.55–27.7 isopycnals

steps.action: They repeat the analysis in the GloSea5 reanalysis (1993–2019): subpolar AMOC correlates with the leading SSH principal component (R = 0.84), and the density and SSH regression patterns again centre on the Irminger Sea.
steps.quote: we turn to an ocean reanalysis to confirm the robustness of the observed sea-surface height and upper-ocean density patterns

steps.action: They check the reanalysis premise by comparing the GloSea5 and OSNAP East AMOC over 2014–2018 (R = 0.73; interannual standard deviations 1.6 vs. 1.82 Sv), and note that the SSH principal components agree partly because GloSea5 assimilates altimetry.
steps.quote: The GloSea5 and OSNAP East AMOC are well correlated, R = 0.73, during the 2014–2018 period

steps.action: They retain Irminger Sea density and SSH as proxies for reconstructing eastern subpolar AMOC variability, and note that these proxies reveal no mechanism.
steps.quote: can thus be used with confidence to reconstruct and diagnose AMOC variability in the eastern SPNA

steps.action: They ask what sets Irminger Sea density, prompted by the mismatch between the location of the density signal (Irminger Sea) and the location of maximum buoyancy loss (Labrador Sea).
steps.quote: In this section, we investigate the origin of the Irminger Sea upper-ocean density.

steps.action: They lay out candidate mechanisms: local atmospheric forcing; the NAO acting through Labrador Sea heat loss and deep-water formation (from modelling studies); and gyre advection of Labrador Sea buoyancy-loss anomalies into the Irminger Sea.
steps.quote: effects of buoyancy loss in the Labrador Sea have the potential to subsequently impact Irminger Sea upper ocean density via the subpolar gyre circulation

steps.action: They take the leading EOF of NCEP/NCAR wind-stress curl (NAO-like), regress density and net heat flux onto it, and correlate it with Irminger Sea density: it explains 40% (interannual-to-decadal) and 67% (multidecadal) of the variance and leads density by 1 year.
steps.quote: This NAO-like variability is found to explain 40% (67%) of the observed Irminger Sea density variability on interannual-to-decadal (multidecadal) timescales

steps.action: They set aside local heat loss as the driver, because the largest density anomalies (Irminger Sea) and the largest NAO-related heat losses (Labrador Sea) fall in different places.
steps.quote: While positive density changes are largest near the Irminger Sea region, the strongest heat losses are found in the Labrador Sea

steps.action: Prompted by the 1-year lag, they design a backward Lagrangian test (TRACMASS on altimetry-derived geostrophic velocities, 4-year trajectories released in 2016) of where Irminger Sea and Iceland Basin waters come from.
steps.quote: To investigate this potential mechanism, we perform a backward Lagrangian analysis based on altimetry-derived geostrophic velocities

steps.action: They compare particle pathways: Labrador-origin particles reaching the Irminger Sea cross the gyre interior within closed dynamic height contours (median transit about 2 years), whereas those reaching the Iceland Basin follow the boundary currents.
steps.quote: This provides observational evidence of advective pathways directly linking the Labrador Sea with the Irminger Sea via the interior of the gyre.

steps.action: They backtrack particles to the subtropics and show that subtropical-origin water stays in the boundary currents and barely reaches the interior Irminger Basin, which makes it unlikely as the source of interior density anomalies.
steps.quote: these trajectories communicate minimally and only occasionally (possibly through eddy stirring) with the interior Irminger Basin

steps.action: They retain the mechanism: interior Labrador Sea water, cooled during strong NAO periods, spreads into the interior Irminger Sea and preconditions the subpolar overturning.
steps.quote: [...] result provides evidence that water from the interior of the Labrador Sea spreads into the interior Irminger Sea

steps.action: They compute the 1950–2019 trend in EN4 Irminger Sea density (−0.005 kg/m3 per decade) and convert it with the OSNAP density–AMOC regression slope to a weakening of about 2.2 Sv (13%), not significant under the modified Mann-Kendall test.
steps.quote: this decline implies a weakening of ∼2.2 Sv or 13% over this period

steps.action: They set the estimate against published reconstructions: Caesar et al. (2018) gives 3 ± 1 Sv; Fraser & Cunningham, Rossby et al., Orvik, Fu et al. and Jackson et al. find no significant change. They conclude there is no consensus on a basin-wide slowdown.
steps.quote: Taken together, we conclude that there is yet no consensus regarding basin-wide North Atlantic slowdown of the overturning circulation.

steps.action: They conclude that the Irminger Sea is the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability, that the NAO drives it via the Labrador Sea and the gyre, and that this challenges the cold-SST/weak-AMOC paradigm.
steps.quote: the Irminger Sea is herein highlighted as the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability

tree.answer: An Irminger Sea density/SSH signature of OSNAP East AMOC strength
AMOC observed directly only for 2014–2018; long-term AMOC only through a proxy
An AMOC fingerprint and indicator, plus its mechanism
Local heat loss vs. Labrador Sea advection via the gyre vs. subtropical NAC origin
Location and lag of density anomalies; Lagrangian pathways into the gyre interior
Conditions found (natural variability, existing observations and reanalyses)

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: interannual-to-multidecadal swings repeat across 2014–2018, 1993–2019 and 1950–2019
Pattern holds in GloSea5 and in SSH principal-component regression; long-term trend not significant
Irminger Sea center of action kept; weakening suggestive but insignificant

end.claim: On interannual-to-decadal timescales, subpolar AMOC strength at OSNAP East covaries with 0–1,000 m density and SSH in the Irminger Sea, which is therefore the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability (OSNAP 2014–2018, GloSea5 1993–2019).

decisive_move.sentence: Correlating the directly measured OSNAP East AMOC with gridded upper-ocean density and SSH established the Irminger Sea signature; every later step (reanalysis check, mechanism, 70-year proxy) builds on it.

gates.evidence: Action: all data are pre-existing (OSNAP, EN4, altimetry, GloSea5, NCEP/NCAR). Only the Lagrangian analysis was run to test a stated advection mechanism (p. 7). Claim: the Irminger pattern could have failed to appear in GloSea5 (p. 4), but GloSea5 assimilates altimetry and is not independent of the observations. The trend was tested for significance and failed it (p. 8). Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Empirical orthogonal functions / principal component analysis (eofs library)
Modified Mann-Kendall trend test for autocorrelated data (Hamed & Rao 1998)
Lagrangian particle back-tracking (TRACMASS) on velocity fields

novelty_claims.quote: In the present study, we examine, for the first time, the signature of the overturning in the subpolar North Atlantic (SPNA) that is rooted in [...]

limits: No review file, open discussion, earlier version or Supporting Information was supplied, so Figures S1–S3 and any review-forced changes cannot be checked. The OSNAP AMOC series is a consortium product (coauthors Bacon and Holliday are on Lozier et al. 2019 and F. Li et al. 2021). Step 2 is coded `cited`; `inherited` would also be defensible. The text calls the correlation maps statistically significant but gives no significance thresholds or effective degrees of freedom in the main text (inference: possibly in the SI). GloSea5 assimilates altimetry and likely hydrography, so the reanalysis replication is not fully independent of the observations; the authors note this only for the SSH principal components. The 70-year AMOC estimate applies a regression slope fitted on five years of OSNAP data to 1950–2019; stationarity of that slope is not tested. The Lagrangian test uses surface geostrophic velocities from a single 2016 release, and its ~2-year median transit time is reconciled with the 1-year lag only by appeal to product smoothing. The exclusion of local forcing rests on visual comparison of regression maps. The abstract gives the reanalysis period as 1993–2018 while the Methods give 1993–2019. Sub-claim statuses: NAO-via-Labrador-Sea-and-gyre mechanism, best_explanation; 2.2 Sv (13%) weakening since 1950, estimate_with_resolution (statistically insignificant); challenge to the cold-SST/weak-AMOC paradigm, interpretation, not separately tested.

disagreements.target: Common paradigm from modern and paleo studies that cold North Atlantic SSTs indicate a weakening AMOC (SST proxies, e.g., Caesar [...]
disagreements.support: In OSNAP and GloSea5, strong subpolar AMOC coincides with colder, denser upper-ocean water in the Irminger Sea.
disagreements.quote: challenges the common paradigm from modern and paleo studies that cold sea-surface temperatures in the North Atlantic are associated with a weakening overturning

disagreements.target: Caesar et al. (2018) SST-based AMOC index
disagreements.support: The index tracks the subtropical RAPID AMOC, and subtropical and subpolar overturning lack decadal coherence, so a single SST metric cannot represent the subpolar AMOC.
disagreements.quote: shows a strong decadal covariability and similar trend as the AMOC estimate from the RAPID array in the subtropical North Atlantic

disagreements.target: Caesar et al. (2018) estimate of a 3 ± 1 Sv weakening since the mid-twentieth century
disagreements.support: The Irminger Sea density proxy gives about 2.2 Sv, consistent in size but not statistically significant.
disagreements.quote: [...] inconsistent with the Caesar et al. (2018) estimate of 3 ± 1 Sv since the mid-twentieth century

disagreements.target: Claims of a twentieth-century basin-wide AMOC slowdown
disagreements.support: An insignificant subpolar trend, together with other reconstructions (Fraser & Cunningham 2021; Rossby et al. 2020; Orvik 2022; Fu et al. 2020; Jackson et al. 2022), shows no consensus.
disagreements.quote: Taken together, we conclude that there is yet no consensus regarding basin-wide North Atlantic slowdown of the overturning circulation.

disagreements.support: Density anomalies controlling the AMOC sit in the Irminger Sea; Lagrangian pathways show the Labrador Sea preconditions those waters rather than dominating the overturning.
disagreements.quote: although the Labrador Sea does not dominate the subpolar overturning, it may play a key role in preconditioning the waters

disagreements.target: Literature arguing AMOC fingerprints are unreliable indicators of long-term change (Little et al. 2020; Jackson & Wood 2020; L. Li [...]
disagreements.support: The Irminger Sea density–AMOC relation holds in both OSNAP and GloSea5, which the authors take as grounds for using it as a long-term indicator.
disagreements.quote: However, the strong relationship between Irminger Sea density and subpolar AMOC change present in OSNAP and GloSea5 provides us with a robust, albeit indirect, measure
